==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|clon||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
Coined (in botany) in 1903, based on {{uder|en|grc|κλών||twig}}. Figurative use from the 1970s.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|klōn}}
** {{IPA|en|/kloʊn/|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-clone.ogg|a=US}}
** {{IPA|en|/kləʊn/|a=RP}}
* {{rhymes|en|əʊn|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A living organism (originally a plant) produced asexually from a single ancestor, to which it is [[genetically]] identical.
#: {{ux|en|This new species is a '''clone''' of the mimosa plant.}}
# {{lb|en|cytology}} A group of identical cells derived from a single cell.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1985|author=[[w:Gunther Stent|Gunther S. Stent]]|author2=David A. Weisblat|title=Cell lineage in the development of invertebrate nervous systems|journal=Annual review of neuroscience|volume=8|number=1|page=45
| passage= […] each identified blastomere, and the '''clone''' of its descendant cells, plays a specific role in later development
}}
# A copy or imitation of something already existing, especially when designed to simulate it.
#: {{ux|en|The computer manufacturer produced IBM PC '''clones''' in the 1990s.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A person who is exactly like or very similar to another person, in terms of looks or behavior.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2017|author=Allyson Kennedy|title=Can't Beat the Heart of a Carolina Girl
|passage=Once, on a confident whim, I approached the group of popular girls in an attempt to broaden my circle. Their ringleader took one glance at my new Aeropostale T-shirt and whispered to her '''clones''', “Yeah, Aero's definitely out now.”}}
# {{lb|en|LGBTQ|slang}} A [[Castro clone]].
